q: A producer re-records a bassline from an old song instead of lifting the audio. What is that called?
why: An interpolation, or replay. It uses the composition but not the original recording, so it involves the song's owners and not the recording's.

q: Which machine is widely described as the first commercially available digital sampling instrument?
why: The Fairlight CMI, launched in 1979, an 8-bit system with a five-figure price.

q: How much total sample time did the E-mu SP-1200 have?
why: About 10 seconds of 12-bit sound, 2.5 seconds per pad. Producers worked around it, and the workarounds became the style.

q: Who designed the swing on the Akai MPC60?
why: Roger Linn designed the MPC60 with Akai; it came out in 1988.

q: Which 1991 case was the first US court ruling on sampling?
options: Grand Upright Music v. Warner Bros. Records
why: Grand Upright, over Biz Markie's use of a Gilbert O'Sullivan song. The opinion opens with "Thou shalt not steal."

q: "Get a license or do not sample" comes from which decision?
why: The Sixth Circuit in Bridgeport, about a two-second Funkadelic guitar chord. The Ninth Circuit disagreed in 2016.

q: Is there a rule that samples under six seconds are free to use?
why: It is folklore. No statute or court sets a safe number of seconds.

q: The Kraftwerk "Metall auf Metall" case turned on a sample how long?
why: A roughly two-second rhythm loop, in court since 1999, with EU rulings in 2019 and 2026.

q: How many permissions does clearing a sample of a recording normally take?
why: Two: one from whoever owns the recording and one from whoever owns the song.

q: When did De La Soul's early albums reach streaming services?
why: March 2023, after years of delay tied to their samples.

q: On "Planet Rock", how did Kraftwerk's music get onto the record?
options: It was licensed from a library
why: The parts were replayed, not sampled.

q: The "Sleng Teng" riddim came from where?
options: A preset on a Casio MT-40 keyboard
why: The MT-40's "rock" preset, written by Casio engineer Okuda Hiroko.

q: Which Akai sampler's time-stretch became part of the sound of 1990s jungle?
why: The S950, which could stretch a sample from 1% to 999%.

q: What did the Library of Congress do with "Amen, Brother" in May 2026?
options: Added it to the National Recording Registry
why: It joined the National Recording Registry in the class of 2026.
